newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Suspect admits involvement in Dutch blaze deaths.
newsitem.headline: Suspect admits involvement in Dutch blaze deaths.

text.p: Dutch police said on Sunday one of the suspects they had arrested in connection with a fire in March that killed a Turkish woman and her five children had confessed to being involved in the incident.

In a brief statement, the Hague police said a 25-year-old suspect, with Turkish nationality and Kurdish background, had been detained on June 6 and had admitted involvement in the blaze after an initial interrogation.
The suspect was related to the victims, it added.
The deaths in March caused an outcry among the Netherlands' 25,000-strong Turkish community and prompted a visit from Turkey by a government delegation to oversee the police investigation.
The fire started on the night of March 25, trapping the woman and her five children in their apartment. Her husband and the couple's other five children escaped by jumping from an upstairs window.
Police are still holding other suspects in connection with their investigation into the fire and two separate fire-bombing incidents which happened in the same area on the same night.
